page: Microsoft Azure D64plds_v5 is an ARM-based compute instance built on the Ampere Altra processor architecture featuring 64 physical Neoverse-N1 cores clocked at 3.0 GHz. Unlike simultaneous multithreading configurations, every vCPU maps to a dedicated single-threaded execution core. The instance is provisioned with 128 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core, and includes 2577 GB of integrated local solid-state storage managed under Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark results highlight strong parallel throughput across multi-core workloads, reflected in a top-tier stress-ng multi-core score of 112410.54 and high-throughput Redis operations reaching 84.83 million SET operations per second. Hardware compilation via Clang (46949.0) and ray tracing (56794.0) also position the host in the upper 25th percentile. Cached small-block memory reads achieve 4384.56 GB/s, though uncached large-block transfers moderate to 177.23 GB/s read and 76.55 GB/s write throughput.

Single-threaded execution represents the primary operational tradeoff, with Geekbench single-core scoring in the lower quartile at 1135.0 and weak text-processing performance. Similarly, large-scale LLM inference is constrained by per-core compute limits, reaching only 6.99 prompt tokens per second on 70B parameter models. Qualitatively, the 64 dedicated physical ARM cores paired with sizable bundled local SSD storage offer high core-density economics for multi-threaded tasks that do not depend on x86 vector instruction sets like AVX-512.

This hardware balance aligns effectively with containerized microservices, high-concurrency web backends, CI/CD code compilation clusters, caching layers like Redis, and parallel data parsing workloads requiring local scratch storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D64plds_v5 is a 64-vCPU ARM-based virtual machine powered by 3.0 GHz Ampere Neoverse-N1 physical cores without multithreading. It features 128 GB of RAM at a 2.0 GB per-core allocation alongside 2577 GB of integrated local SSD storage. Benchmark profiles reveal high parallel computation capabilities, evidenced by strong multi-core stress testing, 84.83 million Redis operations per second, and rapid software build performance in Clang. Single-threaded instruction throughput and large-block memory transfers fall into middle and lower tiers, and x86 vector extensions are unsupported. With dedicated physical cores and local disk storage, the D64plds_v5 delivers cost-effective density for parallel CI/CD compilation, in-memory caching, container orchestration, and multi-threaded web infrastructure.
